subject: Biotechnology
title: Farmer Rights and Seed Patents
description: Learn Farmer Rights and Seed Patents in one minute.

hook.text: Farmers saved seeds for 10,000 years — biotech patents made replanting your own harvest illegal.

buildup.text: Monsanto's technology agreements required farmers to buy new seed each year — replanting patented seeds meant a lawsuit.

discovery.text: Bowman v. Monsanto reached the Supreme Court — the farmer lost, affirming patent exhaustion does not cover self-replicating seeds.

twist.text: Terminator technology — seeds engineered to be sterile — was developed but never commercialized due to global outrage.

climax.text: Open-source seed initiatives release varieties without patent restrictions — the Open Source Seed Initiative guards seed freedom.

punchline.text: Who owns the seed owns the food supply — seed patents are biotech's hottest debate.

quiz.question: What did the Bowman v. Monsanto Supreme Court ruling establish?
options: Farmers have the right to save and replant any seeds they purchase
Patent exhaustion does not apply to self-replicating technologies like seeds, so replanting patented seeds is infringement
Monsanto must share its patented seeds with all farmers for free
